transcript.text: A persistent beep on a fridge-freezer is almost always an alarm triggered by one of two things: either the door hasn't sealed properly (letting warm air in), or the temperature has risen above a safe level. First, please check if the freezer door is fully shut and that no food packets are blocking it from sealing tight. Second, look inside to see if your food is still frozen solid or if it's starting to soften. If the food is still frozen but it beeps when you open the door, this may just be a normal 'door ajar' alarm which should stop once closed. If the food is softening, we need to address the cooling issue.
the bottom drawer wasn't pushed in properly last night, a bag was sticking out. ice cream is a bit soft round the edges but everything else is hard

That explains the beeping perfectly: the alarm is designed to warn you when warm air gets in because the door wasn't sealed. The slight softening of the ice cream edges is normal for that kind of brief exposure. Please push the drawer fully back in and tuck the bag away so it doesn't block the seal again. Then press the 'Alarm' or 'Sound' button on your control panel to silence any remaining beeps. Leave the door closed for about 2–3 hours to let the temperature stabilise, then check if the ice cream has firmed up. If it does and the beeping stops, you're all set.
